claims.value: Alerts/native behavior for an honest MVP: keep enemy and Ruptura cues distinct and never rely on color or audio alone. The bundled enemy ladder is 5 minutes (`enemy.finishOrLeave`, 390 seconds), 2 minutes (`enemy.retreat`, 570 seconds), 1 minute (`enemy.oneMinute`, 630 seconds), 15 seconds (`enemy.final15`, 675 seconds), and expected return (`enemy.expectedReturn`, 690 seconds). The Ruptura ladder is optional planning at 10 minutes (`ruptura.plan10`, 2,640 seconds), 5 minutes (`ruptura.finishTrip5`, 2,940 seconds), warning start at 2:30 (`ruptura.warningBegins`, 3,090 seconds), 1 minute (`ruptura.oneMinute`, 3,180 seconds), 30 seconds (`ruptura.thirtySeconds`, 3,210 seconds), 15 seconds (`ruptura.final15`, 3,225 seconds), and impact at 3,240 seconds/next cycle zero. Product controls should include `Full`, `Haptic only`, `Visual only`, category toggles, preview, exit-buffer-derived `TURN BACK NOW`, and `Mute one cycle`; muting suppresses the remainder of that cycle through its ending impact and alerts resume afterward. Absolute local notifications must be replaced after anchor/model/policy changes and deduplicated by sync epoch, definition, event ID, and cycle index. Paused sessions schedule no alerts. Resume and clock correction never replay historical cues; backward time, stale crossings over 5,000 milliseconds, or long gaps require current-state reconciliation, while delayed foreground crossings present only the strongest events at the latest fresh timestamp. Foreground sound/haptic playback also deduplicates occurrence IDs; warning cues use double haptics and return/impact cues use urgent triples. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor is active and restore it afterward; do not use background audio as a keep-alive. Live Activity is a proposal for one armed next event, not an indefinitely self-advancing authority. AlarmKit on iOS 26 may break through Silent mode and Focus, but only after authorization and an explicit `Arm loud enemy-return alarm`/Watch Session action—never an endless implicit 54-minute alarm. Earlier iOS uses normal local notifications; Time Sensitive is separate opt-in and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Accessibility requires text/symbol/border or pattern alongside color, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, no full-screen flashing, no default per-second ticking, and a stable sentence rather than per-second VoiceOver announcements. The frozen project targets iOS `17.0`; its notification, foreground feedback, and screen-awake services exist, but AlarmKit and Live Activity are not present, and none of this is verified end-to-end because no build, tests, simulator run, or install succeeded in the recorded checkpoint.
